{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Exact comparison feedback for smooth convex objectives\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}ZO\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}O01}

Single-objective optimization

Minimize \AtlasInlineMath{f} globally over \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d} and return a point with small objective gap.

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present

\textbf{Gap classes present.} Polynomial gap; Logarithmic gap

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Global minimization; solution concept: Global minimization; task family: Single objective

\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; smoothness: Lipschitz gradient

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} access order: Zeroth-order interface; interface family: Exact comparison; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; query domain: Full space

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic algorithms; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Objective gap

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; mode: Deterministic; mode: Probability

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Minimize \AtlasInlineMath{f} globally over \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d} and return a point with small objective gap.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
\AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}} is differentiable and satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le\beta\|x-y\|_2} for every \AtlasInlineMath{x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f} is globally convex.

A global minimizer \AtlasInlineMath{x_*\in B_2(0,R)} exists; the localization ball does not restrict the function domain.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Any finite point pair \AtlasInlineMath{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d} may be queried, returning \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{sign}(f(x)-f(y))\in\{-1,0,1\}}. Equal values produce zero. Neither the magnitude of the difference nor either function value is revealed.

The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d}, \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}, \AtlasInlineMath{R}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d}. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*}, where \AtlasInlineMath{f_*=\inf_{u\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(u)}. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
One point-pair comparison costs \AtlasInlineMath{1} call. Every repeated comparison and every comparison in a line search is charged. The budget \AtlasInlineMath{T} counts scalar comparison replies.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic}
Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement \AtlasInlineMath{\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon} holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: \AtlasInlineMath{N\le T} on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized}
Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3}.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: \AtlasInlineMath{N\le T} on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

\textbf{Output qualification.} Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Dimension of the variable space \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb{N},\ d\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: Public upper bound on the gradient Lipschitz constant \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\beta>0}.

The object, norm and domain are fixed by the specific inequalities in this profile's model.

\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Localization radius for a global minimizer \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{x_*\in B_2(0,R)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Error target; norm and squared-norm criteria use different thresholds \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{Q}: Smoothness accuracy ratio \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{Q>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{Q=\beta R^2/\varepsilon}

\AtlasInlineMath{x,y,u}: Function arguments and dummy variables in the formulas \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x,y,u\in\mathbb{R}^d}; spherical domains are embedded in \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^{d+1}}.

Admissible ranges are specified separately by the task, model and oracle in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}}: Final algorithm output \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{I}: Complete problem instance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{I\in\mathcal{I}}.

Includes the unknown objective and its admissible feedback distribution or environment law. Public parameters are fixed before the quantifiers.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{I}}: Admissible instance class determined by the eight specification fields in this profile \textbf{Domain:} Instances satisfying the public parameter bounds.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{A}}: Algorithm or strategy \textbf{Domain:} Measurable adaptive strategies allowed in this profile.

The algorithm is selected before the hidden instance.

\AtlasInlineMath{\ell}: Base loss or residual \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\ell:\mathcal{I}\times\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}}\to[0,+\infty]}.

The exact formula appears in this profile's performance-criterion section.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E},\Pr}: Expectation and probability \textbf{Domain:} Evaluated over the algorithmic and feedback randomness specified by this profile's guarantee.

Fix the instance first; aggregate cost and error separately.

\AtlasInlineMath{\inf,\sup}: Infimum and supremum \textbf{Domain:} Evaluated only over the variable sets explicitly specified in the formula.

In the risk definition, the infimum over algorithms precedes the supremum over instances or centers.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\|x\|_2=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\langle x,y\rangle=x^\top y}

\AtlasInlineMath{B_p(c,R)}: Closed norm ball \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{p\in[1,\infty],\ R\ge0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{B_p(c,R)=\{x:\|x-c\|_p\le R\}}; \AtlasInlineMath{B_2} denotes the Euclidean ball.

\AtlasInlineMath{N,T}: Actual call count and declared budget \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N,T\in\mathbb{N}_0}.

A fixed budget bounds every execution path; the Markov specification uses an expected budget.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}}: Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching orders, and upper bounds with hidden logarithms \textbf{Domain:} Within the joint parameter window specified for each complexity regime.

Dependence of hidden constants on fixed parameters is stated separately for each bound. Tilde notation may hide logarithmic factors only in the declared variables.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C,c_\alpha,C_\alpha}: Positive constant in a proof or asymptotic bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c,C,c_\alpha,C_\alpha<\infty}.

Unsubscripted constants have the dependencies stated in the bound; constants subscripted by \AtlasInlineMath{\alpha} may depend only on the fixed smoothness order.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\log_+,e}: Natural logarithm, truncated logarithm, and Euler's number \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{z>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log_+(z)=\max\{0,\log z\}}; \AtlasInlineMath{e=\exp(1)}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\log_2} denotes the base-two logarithm.

\AtlasInlineMath{f,f_*}: Population objective and its optimal value \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{fun}}\to\mathbb{R}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f_*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f,\nabla^2f,D^jf}: Gradient, Hessian, and higher Fréchet derivatives \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla f\in\mathbb{R}^d,\ \nabla^2f\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}}; \AtlasInlineMath{D^jf} is a \AtlasInlineMath{j}-linear form.

Used only at derivative orders and on regions where the model guarantees its existence.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}}: Euclidean induced matrix or tensor operator norm \textbf{Domain:} Take the supremum over Euclidean unit input vectors of the corresponding order.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|}

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{fun}},\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}},\mathcal{X}}: Function domain, admissible output domain and optimization domain \textbf{Domain:} Each is the Euclidean space or subset explicitly specified in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathbb{R}^d} and \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^d}; the function domain is the region on which the model imposes regularity.

\AtlasInlineMath{N^*}: Optimal worst-case oracle complexity satisfying the complete guarantee \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N^*\in[0,+\infty]}.

Take the infimum over admissible algorithms, followed by the worst case over the instances of this profile. With multiple resources, use this scalar only for an explicitly specified resource projection.

\AtlasInlineMath{x_*}: A global minimizer or quadratic center whose existence is promised by the model \textbf{Domain:} Belongs to the localization domain specified here; used only under the stated existence promise.

The full-space minimizer is unique in the strongly convex class. The center of a positive semidefinite quadratic model need not be unique.

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Two exact scalar values simulate one comparison. Therefore a fixed-success exact-value lower bound \$L\$ gives a comparison lower bound \$L/\allowbreak{}2\$. Expected-error targets require a separate constant-factor accuracy conversion.\newline{}\newline{}At each adaptive comparison request \$(x,\allowbreak{}y)\$,\allowbreak{} query both exact values and return their order,\allowbreak{} including the declared tie convention. The same seed and transcript generate the same next query and output,\allowbreak{} using at most twice the comparison budget. Hence a comparison algorithm contradicts a value lower theorem only when all source model and guarantee conditions match.\newline{}\newline{}For smooth convex objectives,\allowbreak{} apply the dimension/\allowbreak{}accuracy branch of Dorn et al.,\allowbreak{} Theorem 2.1,\allowbreak{} at \$Q\textbackslash{}ge32\$,\allowbreak{} and its logarithmic strongly convex subclass at \$Q\textbackslash{}ge128\textasciicircum{}2\$;\allowbreak{} maximize only on their common window. For a strongly convex model with initial gap \$\textbackslash{}Delta\$,\allowbreak{} choose a hard-instance radius \$R\_\allowbreak{}h=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}beta\}\$. Smoothness at the global minimizer gives the required initial gap. If the target guarantee is expected error \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon\$,\allowbreak{} Markov supplies success \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$ at error \$3\textbackslash{}varepsilon\$;\allowbreak{} then the source scale is \$Q\_\allowbreak{}h=\allowbreak{}2\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}(3\textbackslash{}varepsilon)\$ and must be at least 32. No new public radius is added to the target specification.\newline{}\newline{}For nonconvex gradient stationarity,\allowbreak{} use the exact-value hard subclass with a proof-only Lipschitz budget satisfying \$L\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta\$. The source cap \$B=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta,\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}\}\$ becomes \$\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta\$. Retain its small-gradient window and dimension requirement \$d\textbackslash{}ge C(\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textasciicircum{}2)\textbackslash{}log(2+\textbackslash{}beta\textbackslash{}Delta/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textasciicircum{}2)\$. The same two-value simulation then gives the registered comparison lower bound.\par\endgroup

Source n=\allowbreak{}d,\allowbreak{}L=\allowbreak{}beta. A native tie0 is mapped to +1,\allowbreak{} an allowed source tie reply. Finite positive probes and Euclidean projection use only native public inputs;\allowbreak{} no value or certificate is obtained. The following explicit estimator supplies the needed direction guarantee independently of implementation details in source Algorithm2.\newline{}\newline{}Complete direction-estimation construction:\allowbreak{} Given delta in(0,\allowbreak{}1],\allowbreak{} gamma>0,\allowbreak{} use tolerance tau=\allowbreak{}delta gamma/\allowbreak{}(100d\textasciicircum{}2). A comparison at (x+(2tau/\allowbreak{}beta)v,\allowbreak{}x),\allowbreak{} for unit v,\allowbreak{} yields either <grad f(x),\allowbreak{}v>>=\allowbreak{}-tau or <grad f(x),\allowbreak{}v><=\allowbreak{}tau;\allowbreak{} this follows immediately from the smoothness Taylor remainder bounded by beta h\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} and is source Lemma1. Orient each basis vector v\_\allowbreak{}i=\allowbreak{}+/\allowbreak{}-e\_\allowbreak{}i using this test,\allowbreak{} so a\_\allowbreak{}i=\allowbreak{}<grad f,\allowbreak{}v\_\allowbreak{}i>>=\allowbreak{}-tau. Find a pivot p by a sequential tournament:\allowbreak{} compare components with direction (v\_\allowbreak{}i-v\_\allowbreak{}j)/\allowbreak{}sqrt(2);\allowbreak{} the selected winner is at least the loser minus sqrt(2)tau. If ||grad f||>=\allowbreak{}gamma,\allowbreak{} max a\_\allowbreak{}i>=\allowbreak{}||grad f||/\allowbreak{}sqrt(d),\allowbreak{} and the final pivot a\_\allowbreak{}p>=\allowbreak{}max a\_\allowbreak{}i-sqrt(2)(d-1)tau>=\allowbreak{}gamma/\allowbreak{}(2sqrt(d))>0. Moreover each ratio r\_\allowbreak{}i=\allowbreak{}a\_\allowbreak{}i/\allowbreak{}a\_\allowbreak{}p lies in[-2,\allowbreak{}2],\allowbreak{} because a\_\allowbreak{}i>=\allowbreak{}-tau and a\_\allowbreak{}i<=\allowbreak{}a\_\allowbreak{}p+2d tau. For i!=\allowbreak{}p bisect [-2,\allowbreak{}2] using the directional test on (z v\_\allowbreak{}p-v\_\allowbreak{}i)/\allowbreak{}sqrt(1+z\textasciicircum{}2). Each reply compares z with r\_\allowbreak{}i up to kappa=\allowbreak{}sqrt(5)tau/\allowbreak{}a\_\allowbreak{}p<=\allowbreak{}2sqrt(5)sqrt(d)tau/\allowbreak{}gamma<=\allowbreak{}delta/\allowbreak{}(16sqrt(d)). Keep the indicated half interval;\allowbreak{} inductively the true r\_\allowbreak{}i stays within distance kappa of it. After K=\allowbreak{}ceil(log\_\allowbreak{}2(32sqrt(d)/\allowbreak{}delta)) rounds,\allowbreak{} its midpoint alpha\_\allowbreak{}i satisfies |alpha\_\allowbreak{}i-r\_\allowbreak{}i|<=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}2\textasciicircum{}K+kappa<=\allowbreak{}delta/\allowbreak{}(8sqrt(d)). Set alpha\_\allowbreak{}p=\allowbreak{}1. The vector r=\allowbreak{}(a\_\allowbreak{}i/\allowbreak{}a\_\allowbreak{}p) has norm>=\allowbreak{}1;\allowbreak{} ||alpha-r||<=\allowbreak{}delta/\allowbreak{}8. The elementary normalization inequality ||u/\allowbreak{}||u||-v/\allowbreak{}||v||||<=\allowbreak{}2||u-v||/\allowbreak{}||v|| shows that h=\allowbreak{}(sum alpha\_\allowbreak{}i v\_\allowbreak{}i)/\allowbreak{}||alpha|| differs from grad f/\allowbreak{}||grad f|| by at most delta/\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{} hence at most delta. For d=\allowbreak{}1 the ratio loop is empty and the oriented sign is correct under the promise. With or without the promise,\allowbreak{} the schedule has d+(d-1)+(d-1)K=\allowbreak{}O(d log(d/\allowbreak{}delta)) comparisons and returns a unit vector because alpha\_\allowbreak{}p=\allowbreak{}1. Every probing radius is positive and finite,\allowbreak{} and no unbounded line search occurs.\newline{}\newline{}Complete uniform optimization derivation:\allowbreak{} Let Q=\allowbreak{}beta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}epsilon>=\allowbreak{}32,\allowbreak{} T=\allowbreak{}ceil(128Q),\allowbreak{} delta=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}(16 sqrt(Q)),\allowbreak{} gamma=\allowbreak{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}(2R),\allowbreak{} eta=\allowbreak{}R/\allowbreak{}sqrt(T). Start x\_\allowbreak{}0=\allowbreak{}0;\allowbreak{} at each t=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}T-1 get unit h\_\allowbreak{}t from the explicit fixed-schedule estimator above and set x\_\allowbreak{}\{t+1\}=\allowbreak{}Proj\_\allowbreak{}\{B\_\allowbreak{}R\}(x\_\allowbreak{}t-eta h\_\allowbreak{}t). Select the minimum-value point among x\_\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}\{T-1\} by T-1 charged comparisons. This never needs a function value or optimality certificate. Suppose every recorded point has gap g\_\allowbreak{}t>epsilon. Convexity gives ||grad f(x\_\allowbreak{}t)||>=\allowbreak{}g\_\allowbreak{}t/\allowbreak{}||x\_\allowbreak{}t-x\_\allowbreak{}*||>=\allowbreak{}epsilon/\allowbreak{}(2R),\allowbreak{} so all estimates satisfy their promise. Smoothness and the global infimum give ||grad f(x)||\textasciicircum{}2<=\allowbreak{}2 beta (f(x)-f\_\allowbreak{}*):\allowbreak{} apply the descent inequality to x-grad f(x)/\allowbreak{}beta. Consequently <h\_\allowbreak{}t,\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}t-x\_\allowbreak{}*>>=\allowbreak{}g\_\allowbreak{}t/\allowbreak{}||grad f(x\_\allowbreak{}t)||-2R delta>=\allowbreak{}(1/\allowbreak{}sqrt(2)-1/\allowbreak{}8)R/\allowbreak{}sqrt(Q). The projection inequality telescopes to (1/\allowbreak{}T)sum\_\allowbreak{}t <h\_\allowbreak{}t,\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}t-x\_\allowbreak{}*><=\allowbreak{}R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(2 eta T)+eta/\allowbreak{}2=\allowbreak{}R/\allowbreak{}sqrt(T)<=\allowbreak{}R/\allowbreak{}sqrt(128Q),\allowbreak{} a contradiction. Thus the tournament output has gap <=\allowbreak{}epsilon. The deterministic worst-case cost is T O(d log(d/\allowbreak{}delta))+(T-1)=\allowbreak{}O(dQ log(dQ)),\allowbreak{} with universal constants,\allowbreak{} uniform in d,\allowbreak{}beta,\allowbreak{}R,\allowbreak{}epsilon. The same deterministic strategy is admissible for randomized g1,\allowbreak{} with success probability one;\allowbreak{} no random selection or amplification is needed. This also avoids the t=\allowbreak{}0 step-size notation in the printed Algorithm 3.\newline{}\newline{}Cutting-plane audit:\allowbreak{} v1 Theorem 1 requires a genuine lower bound gamma on the gradient norm. Theorem 3 (printed p9) instead supplies gamma=\allowbreak{}sqrt(2 beta epsilon);\allowbreak{} its displayed convexity argument supplies only gap/\allowbreak{}(2R) (or gap/\allowbreak{}(3R) for a general point in B\_\allowbreak{}\{2R\}),\allowbreak{} which does not imply that gamma. Explicit admissible witness for Q>=\allowbreak{}32:\allowbreak{} f(x)=\allowbreak{}(2epsilon/\allowbreak{}R\textasciicircum{}2)||x-R e\_\allowbreak{}1||\textasciicircum{}2. Its gradient Lipschitz constant 4epsilon/\allowbreak{}R\textasciicircum{}2 is <=\allowbreak{}beta,\allowbreak{} its minimizer is R e\_\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} and at x=\allowbreak{}0 it has gap 2epsilon and gradient norm 4epsilon/\allowbreak{}R < sqrt(2 beta epsilon). Thus a nonoptimal query need not satisfy the estimator's promise. Also the full epsilon/\allowbreak{}2-sublevel need not be bounded by B\_\allowbreak{}\{2R\};\allowbreak{} the constant objective is a simple example. A valid localization proof must intersect with a known ball and handle its boundary. Finally,\allowbreak{} the displayed cost is [C d log(dR/\allowbreak{}r\_\allowbreak{}K)] times [O(d log(d/\allowbreak{}delta))] plus a tournament. With r\_\allowbreak{}K=\allowbreak{}R/\allowbreak{}sqrt(Q) and delta=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}(16sqrt(Q)),\allowbreak{} its direct product is O(d\textasciicircum{}2 log\textasciicircum{}2(dQ)),\allowbreak{} not the claimed single logarithm. These are failures of the supplied justification,\allowbreak{} not a theorem that the true minimax upper rate cannot be smaller. Quarantine the combined b1 claims;\allowbreak{} do not adopt a repaired cutting-plane rate without a complete new localization/\allowbreak{}separation proof.\newline{}\newline{}Endpoint checks:\allowbreak{} R,\allowbreak{}beta,\allowbreak{}epsilon are positive and d>=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} so there is no Q=\allowbreak{}0 endpoint in the contract. Smoothness at x\_\allowbreak{}* gives f(0)-f\_\allowbreak{}*<=\allowbreak{}beta R\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}2;\allowbreak{} hence returning 0 uses zero queries when Q<=\allowbreak{}2. This elementary check is outside all four registered comparison regions and is not added here as a native endpoint bound/\allowbreak{}comparison. For Q>=\allowbreak{}32 our fixed schedule applies also at d=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} with no precision-independent saturation assertion. At Q=\allowbreak{}d\textasciicircum{}2 the c1/\allowbreak{}c2 lower formulas both equal Omega(d\textasciicircum{}2);\allowbreak{} c1 owns equality.\par\endgroup

Smoothness and a point x*{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ∈}\allowbreak{}B\_\allowbreak{}R give B(x*,\allowbreak{}r){\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ⊂}\allowbreak{}K{\AtlasUnicodeText ε}\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} because r{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ≤}\allowbreak{}R and {\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ∇}\allowbreak{}f(x*)=\allowbreak{}0.\newline{}\newline{}Starting from C0=\allowbreak{}B(0,\allowbreak{}2R),\allowbreak{} at each iteration take the center of gravity x of the current known convex body,\allowbreak{} run the direction estimator above with {\AtlasUnicodeText γ}\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}{\AtlasUnicodeText ε}\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}(3R) and {\AtlasUnicodeText δ}\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}(48Q),\allowbreak{} and retain C{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ∩}\allowbreak{}\{y:\allowbreak{}<h,\allowbreak{}y{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols −}\allowbreak{}x>{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ≤}\allowbreak{}0\}. For every y{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ∈}\allowbreak{}K{\AtlasUnicodeText ε}\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} ||y{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols −}\allowbreak{}x||{\AtlasUnicodeSymbols ≤}\allowbreak{}4R and\newline{}\newline{}\textbackslash{}[\newline{}\textbackslash{}langle h,\allowbreak{}y-x\textbackslash{}rangle\newline{}\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}frac\{f(y)-f(x)\}\{\textbackslash{}|\textbackslash{}nabla f(x)\textbackslash{}|\}+4R\textbackslash{}delta\newline{}<-\textbackslash{}frac\{\textbackslash{}varepsilon\}\{6\textbackslash{}beta R\}+\textbackslash{}frac\{\textbackslash{}varepsilon\}\{12\textbackslash{}beta R\}<0.\newline{}\textbackslash{}]\newline{}\newline{}Thus every bad cut retains the inner ball. After the fixed number of iterations\newline{}\newline{}\textbackslash{}[\newline{}N=\allowbreak{}1+\textbackslash{}left\textbackslash{}lceil\textbackslash{}frac\{d\textbackslash{}log(2\textbackslash{}sqrt Q)\}\{-\textbackslash{}log(1-1/\allowbreak{}e)\}\textbackslash{}right\textbackslash{}rceil\newline{}\textbackslash{}]\newline{}\newline{}if all iterations were still bad,\allowbreak{} the remaining volume would be smaller than that of a ball of radius r,\allowbreak{} a contradiction.
